summary: /en/deconstructing writes «Worker» in code format in its prose, like the Spanish page and every other stack name.

changes.before: When you type the address, `Cloudflare`'s DNS answers. The zone is signed with `DNSSEC`, a signature that lets anyone check the answer was not altered on the way. The connection is encrypted with TLS 1.3 at the least, and in browsers that support it not even the site's name travels in the clear. On the other side there is no server of our own: a Worker answers, a program `Cloudflare` runs in the data centre closest to the visitor.
changes.after: When you type the address, `Cloudflare`'s DNS answers. The zone is signed with `DNSSEC`, a signature that lets anyone check the answer was not altered on the way. The connection is encrypted with TLS 1.3 at the least, and in browsers that support it not even the site's name travels in the clear. On the other side there is no server of our own: a `Worker` answers, a program `Cloudflare` runs in the data centre closest to the visitor.

changes.before: Each domain is a [`Custom Domain`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/custom-domains/): the Worker is the origin and there is no server behind it. The certificate is issued and renewed automatically.
changes.after: Each domain is a [`Custom Domain`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/custom-domains/): the `Worker` is the origin and there is no server behind it. The certificate is issued and renewed automatically.

changes.before: In front of the Worker sits `Cloudflare`'s cache, which keeps copies of pages in each data centre. If the page you ask for is already stored, it is delivered without running the Worker. Only pages that ask for it are stored, and publishing a change from the content management system (the CMS) clears, by tag, that page and every page that lists it.
changes.after: In front of the `Worker` sits `Cloudflare`'s cache, which keeps copies of pages in each data centre. If the page you ask for is already stored, it is delivered without running the `Worker`. Only pages that ask for it are stored, and publishing a change from the content management system (the CMS) clears, by tag, that page and every page that lists it.

changes.before: [`Workers Cache`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/) sits in front of the Worker and is tiered by default: a hit does not run the Worker.
changes.after: [`Workers Cache`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/) sits in front of the `Worker` and is tiered by default: a hit does not run the `Worker`.

before.text: An expired copy is served at once and rebuilt behind the request, for up to a week. Nobody waits for the Worker except after a deploy, after that page is published, or after a week without visits. These rules live in the Worker, because the zone's cache rules do not reach `Workers Cache`.

after.text: An expired copy is served at once and rebuilt behind the request, for up to a week. Nobody waits for the `Worker` except after a deploy, after that page is published, or after a week without visits. These rules live in the `Worker`, because the zone's cache rules do not reach `Workers Cache`.

before.text: When the pointer rests on an internal link, the browser asks for that page in advance. If it was not stored, the Worker renders it then, and the click finds it in the cache. `Cloudflare`'s own prefetch, `Speed Brain`, does not apply here: it never prefetches a page that runs a Worker.

after.text: When the pointer rests on an internal link, the browser asks for that page in advance. If it was not stored, the `Worker` renders it then, and the click finds it in the cache. `Cloudflare`'s own prefetch, `Speed Brain`, does not apply here: it never prefetches a page that runs a `Worker`.

changes.before: The whole site is produced by a single Worker with `Astro`, a framework that assembles each page at the moment it is requested. Files that never change, such as styles, scripts and images, are served directly, without running any code. There is no server behind it, and before answering the Worker adds seven security headers to every page.
changes.after: The whole site is produced by a single `Worker` with `Astro`, a framework that assembles each page at the moment it is requested. Files that never change, such as styles, scripts and images, are served directly, without running any code. There is no server behind it, and before answering the `Worker` adds seven security headers to every page.

changes.before: One [`Worker`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/astro/) renders the pages on demand with `Astro` (SSR). The built files are served as [`Workers Static Assets`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/) without running it. There is no server behind the Worker.
changes.after: One [`Worker`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/framework-guides/web-apps/astro/) renders the pages on demand with `Astro` (SSR). The built files are served as [`Workers Static Assets`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/) without running it. There is no server behind the `Worker`.

changes.before: One middleware stamps 7 security headers on every page the Worker renders. The CSP admits one outside script and no other: the visit counter from `Cloudflare`.
changes.after: One middleware stamps 7 security headers on every page the `Worker` renders. The CSP admits one outside script and no other: the visit counter from `Cloudflare`.

changes.before: The Worker knows the visitor's city and which `Cloudflare` data centre answered (`request.cf`). The edge-security opening shows them.
changes.after: The `Worker` knows the visitor's city and which `Cloudflare` data centre answered (`request.cf`). The edge-security opening shows them.

changes.before: The site's CMS is `EmDash`, `Cloudflare`'s open-source content management system, and it runs inside the same Worker that serves the pages. Its admin edits pages, services, menus and every interface label, in Spanish and English. On publishing, a plugin kept in the repository clears what changed from the cache.
changes.after: The site's CMS is `EmDash`, `Cloudflare`'s open-source content management system, and it runs inside the same `Worker` that serves the pages. Its admin edits pages, services, menus and every interface label, in Spanish and English. On publishing, a plugin kept in the repository clears what changed from the cache.

changes.before: `EmDash`, the open-source (MIT) CMS that `Cloudflare` announced in April 2026, runs inside the same Worker.
changes.after: `EmDash`, the open-source (MIT) CMS that `Cloudflare` announced in April 2026, runs inside the same `Worker`.
